bug: T65: logged sets carried the parser's unit, and the parser's rulebook said an unlabelled load is lbs (this app's default). A kg athlete's 'squat 5x3 at 140' could be saved as a 140 LB squat, and in practice the parser sometimes carried kg across lifts and sometimes did not. These are the founder's real rows (read-only copies, 2026-09-29) run through the T65 resolver.
source: Founder account 0704b840-45db-4bff-81eb-064154092e7f (weight_unit kg, writes kg since 2026-08-17). Copied read-only; nothing was repaired.

rows.name: 09-04 C&J + back squat: parser carried kg onto unlabelled ladders
rows.raw_message:
Day 5 – Clean & Jerk/Back Squat

Clean and Jerk singles @ 70/90/100/110/120/130
Back Squat singles @ 70/110/130/150/170 then I missed 180kg

expect_if_lbs_athlete.why: an lbs athlete: 180kg is written on the squat only, so the squat ladder is kg (same lift) and the C&J ladder follows the athlete (T46: a unit never carries to the next lift)

rows.name: 08-18 bench ladder, no unit written, stored lbs
rows.raw_message:
Day 2 – Bench/Dips

Bench 5x2 @ 185/205/205 (stopped because I felt it in my pec) I’ll have to go slower and with less weight in the future
Dips 3x6 (bodyweight, upper arm to parallel only, no deep stretch) I did these assisted because my pec is hurting
rows.note: The one barbell lift stored as lbs with no unit written since the switch. It was most likely right as lbs (the founder benches in lbs: 245 lb single on 08-10, 275 lb max on file). T65 files it in the athlete's unit (205 kg), and the T46 implausible-jump guard then holds it back and asks, because 205 kg x2 is far past a 275 lb max. The guard compares both in lbs.
